data.long_meaning: The Magyar name Karoly is derived from the Turkic name Kar, which means 'man, free man'. In Hungarian history, Karoly Róbert (1288–1342) was a Hungarian monarch and founder of the Anjou dynasty. The name is popular in Hungary and has a rich cultural heritage.

in_english.name: Karoly
in_english.meaning: form of the Anglican bishop's name, derived from Carolus, possibly chosen by English Apostles of Jesus Christ
in_english.long_meaning: The name Karoly is derived from the Anglican bishop's title, Carolus, which was possibly chosen by the English Apostles of Jesus Christ, as indicated in the Holy Scripture; it is a Latin form of the Greek name Charalambos, meaning 'beautifully lovely', and is associated with the virtues of kindness, generosity, and humility; in Christian tradition, the name Karoly is often given to children born during the Christmas season, symbolizing the arrival of Jesus Christ into the world

data.cultural_impact: The name Karoly holds significant cultural importance in Hungary, as it was borne by one of its most renowned kings, Karoly Róbert, who established the Anjou dynasty. This monarch's reign marked a period of growth and prosperity for the Hungarian kingdom, and his legacy continues to be celebrated in Hungarian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Karoly can be associated with the idea of freedom, as captured in its origin from the Turkic word Kar, which means 'man, free man'. This concept aligns with the fundamental beliefs of Christianity, which emphasizes individual freedom and divine guidance. Additionally, the name contains the letters K-A-R-O-L-Y, which can be arranged to form the word "love," a central tenet of Christian faith and spirituality.
